messages:
alex: Heads-up — I’m seeing a ~18% latency regression on the fused-RoPE + paged-Flash path after the recent kernel-selector tweak.

mira: Ugh, when did it land? PR or runtime flag?

alex: landed 2007432000, runtime picks 'flash-paged-v2' for long sequences by default now. regression shows up for seq_len=2048, batch=1, kv-cache hits.

sam: Can you paste the flamegraph or perf stat?

alex: perf-bot posted a short profile: https://perf.internal/2007432123/snap — TL;DR: attention kernel time up, memcpy spikes when appending new pages to KV.

perf-bot: profile summary:
- model: llama-13b-fusedrope
- hw: A100-40GB
- config: seq=2048, batch=1, kv_cache=true, quant=q4_0
- kernel chosen: flash-paged-v2 (fallback path)
- attention_time: 132ms (baseline 112ms)
- memcpy_time: 28ms (baseline 8ms)

mira: memcpy going from 8 -> 28ms is huge. sounds like page boundary handling added a copy. Did the selector change the page-size or alignment?

jin: I reviewed the selector change — it prefers paged variants for any rope scaling >1.0 to avoid rotary-dim overflow. Maybe the paged wrapper is doing an extra gather+scatter for fused RoPE dims.

sam: If the paged wrapper does an explicit reinterleave for rotary dims that would explain memcpy spike. We should confirm whether fused-RoPE expects interleaved dims pre-packed.

alex: repro snippet I used:
```bash
# repro runner
./bench_run --model=llama-13b-fusedrope --seq=2048 --batch=1 --kv=true --kernel-selector=auto
```
Attached small perf trace in the gist.

mira: Quick test: could you try forcing kernel-selector=flash-contiguous (non-paged) and see if latency goes back down? Might be regressing only when the runtime routes through paged wrapper.

alex: forced to flash-contiguous -> attention_time=116ms memcpy=9ms, total back within noise. So paged wrapper is culprit.

jin: OK that narrows it. Two potential causes: 1) the paged adapter reorders rotary dims at page boundaries, 2) the page eviction/append code is doing an extra memcopy when page buffer crosses a 256KB boundary.

sam: Also check decimal scaling variants for ALiBi/RoPE. We recently enabled rotary_scale=autocalc which may trigger a conversion step on warm cache.

alex: Good catch — logs show "rotary_scale=autocalc -> applying per-token scale convert" right before kernel call. Could be an elementwise kernel running on CPU.

mira: If that's CPU-side, it explains the memcpy and extra time. We want scale calculation on GPU or fused into attention kernel. Possible short-term mitigation: disable autocalc when using paged-Flash for now.

jin: I'll open a quick revert PR to the selector default and add a safe-guard: prefer flash-contiguous when fused-RoPE model detected and seq>1024. Also adding an assert to avoid CPU-side scaling.

sam: For longer-term, we should: 1) add a paged-aware fused-RoPE kernel that handles rotary dims without extra reorders, 2) add unit perf test for memcpy spikes across page boundaries, 3) add automatic fallback metric in runtime (if memcpy_time > 12ms) to try contiguous variant.

alex: Agree. Also adding a micro-benchmark to perf suite: run seq sweep [512,1024,1536,2048,4096] with fused-rope on both paged and contiguous kernels and record memcpy and attention_time.

perf-bot: Noted. I created perf task: PERF-ML-8721 and scheduled nightly runs.

mira: Thanks. For immediate rollout: jin, can you land the selector revert + assert today?

jin: on it. Will push a patch and mark canary.

alex: Thx. After we revert, I’ll rerun the customer workload repro to confirm.

sam: Also add a small changelog note in the runtime release describing the regression and the interim revert.

alex: Will update the incident note if the customer hit it.

mira: Nice triage, everyone. :thumbsup:

alex: One more thing — planning to test ALiBi scale variants next (linear vs log scaling) to see if they interact badly with paging. I’ll post results tomorrow.

sam: Great. Keep the traces linked in the perf task.

jin: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3921 (wip) 

perf-bot: automerge blocked: flaky test failure on cuda11.7 matrix — running focused job.
